newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford says to recommend Avonmore merger.
newsitem.headline: Waterford says to recommend Avonmore merger.

text.p: Ireland's Waterford Foods Plc and the Waterford Co-op said on Tuesday they had decided to recommend to their members a revised offer from Avonmore Foods for the two companies to merge.
It said the total value of Avonmore's offer was 337 million Irish pounds.

"The boards of Avonmore and Waterford believe that the proposed merger is in the best interests of the shareholders and milk suppliers in both organisations and are aware that there is a consensus at goverment and industry levels that the Irish dairy sector needs to further consolidate," the two companies said in a statement.

They said the merger offer valued Waterford Foods shares at 142p, compared with a closing price of 110p on the Dublin stock market on Monday, and a price of 80p on April 10 before Waterford announced it had received an approach from Avonmore.
Avonmore's previous merger offer, which valued Waterford at 281 million pounds ($460.1 million), was rejected by Waterford.
The merger will create the largest dairy group in Britain and Ireland, and the fourth-largest milk producer in the world, analysts said.
